claims.text: As-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain and toughness than commercially used pure tungsten.
The plastic strain and toughness of as-cast WTaTiVZr are primarily governed by its solidification-induced dual-phase dendritic microstructure.
The alloy contains an interlocking network of W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions.
The dendritic network promotes localized plastic deformation.
The dendritic network retards crack propagation by enhancing grain-boundary cohesion and modifying dislocation motion.
The as-cast alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr and is produced by arc melting with at least five remelts.
The pure-tungsten comparator is powder-sintered and has coarse equiaxed grains of approximately 100 ± 20 µm.
The solidification-segregated microstructure consists of two BCC phases.
Vanadium is distributed between the W-Ta-rich and Zr-Ti-rich phases.
The W-Ta-rich dendrites provide high strength through multicomponent solid-solution strengthening.
The Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions enhance dislocation mobility.
The Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions strengthen grain boundaries.
The dual-phase mechanism lowers the brittle-to-ductile transition temperature by enabling localized plastic flow and dissipating stress concentrations.
WTaTiVZr will have higher yield strength than pure tungsten at room and elevated temperatures.
WTaTiVZr will have greater plastic strain than pure tungsten, particularly above approximately 200°C.
WTaTiVZr will have a lower brittle-to-ductile transition temperature than pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will show less scratch-induced cracking and higher scratch-derived fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The pure-tungsten baseline has an indentation-derived yield strength of approximately 700 MPa at room temperature and 250 MPa at 500°C.
The pure-tungsten baseline has negligible plasticity below approximately 300°C.
The pure-tungsten baseline has a scratch-derived fracture toughness of approximately 25 ± 1 MPa√m.

contradictions.description: The proposed comparison is said to isolate the dual-phase microstructure, but it simultaneously changes composition, manufacturing route, grain morphology, and phase constitution between arc-melted WTaTiVZr and powder-sintered tungsten. Thus, it cannot uniquely attribute a mechanical difference to the dendritic microstructure.
